what: Splits the screen into 5×8px cells with a fixed-width character in each (01<>[]{}()/\|=+*#%&$@!?;…:.~ABCDEF0-9) flickering, it spreads in blob order (6×4 noise delay 0~.88) to cover the panel, then clears in a different blob order — cover and clear each take 720ms of linear progress. Each cell is on for 12% of the total, and cells that are on for more than 35% also lay down a background-color plate to hide the screen behind. Characters in cells turning on are crisp, fully-on cells breathe between .35~.85 opacity, and each cell’s character changes on a 70~190ms period (every 19th flashes). Used as a page transition panel via fx:cover → swap section → fx:reveal, and with links: on it hooks same-site link navigation (the next document opens covered and then clears)

options.dur: Duration of one cover or uncover, default 720 ms
options.reduced-dur: Length (ms) of the fade to the background color when motion is reduced, default 180
options.links: With on, it intercepts presses on same-site a[href], covers the page, then navigates, and the cover lifts away on the new document
options.--fx-curtain-bg: Veil background color (css), default a 6:4 mix of the base and the light surface — original #eaeaec
options.fx:cover / fx:reveal: Event sent to an element — if detail.done is present it is called when finished. When done, the element emits fx:covered / fx:revealed

from.where: shared.js section transitions (Index, wheel, keys) and page transitions — original data-ascii-curtain canvas (CURTAIN_DURATION_MS 720 · cell innerWidth/5 × innerHeight/8 · CELL_FADE_WINDOW .12 · background threshold .35)

note: Text color reads the element’s color (default --kf-ink), curtain background reads --fx-curtain-bg when painted on the canvas. On large screens there are about 30k cells, so only 1/48 of the letters are redrawn each frame
